title: Prepare Data for BHF Model — prepare_bhf_data
text: data data frame containing survey data. outcome Character string. Name binary outcome variable (0/1). domain Character string. Name domain/state variable. strata Character string. Name stratification variable. psu Character string. Name PSU (primary sampling unit) variable. weights Character string. Name survey weight variable. population_shares Optional named positive numeric vector whose names exactly match observed complete-case domains. Values normalized sum one canonical domain order. NULL, shares estimated retained raw survey weights. weight_scaling Likelihood-weight scaling method. default "mean_one" scales raw weights globally sum retained sample size. "legacy_d2" warned sensitivity/reproduction path. deattenuation Character mode: "taylor" (default), "supplied", "none". sampling_variances Named nonnegative domain sampling variances deattenuation = "supplied". sampling_variance_method Provenance label supplied variances: "external_taylor", "external_replicate", "external_other". use_deattenuation Deprecated logical compatibility argument. Use deattenuation instead. prior_alpha_mean Numeric. Prior mean intercept logit scale. Default NULL, estimates data. prior_alpha_sd Numeric. Prior SD intercept. Default 0.5. sigma_state_prior Article prior-sensitivity selector state random-effect SD. Exactly one "half_t3_2.5" (baseline), "half_normal_1", "half_cauchy_2.5", "half_t3_5". Stratum PSU SD priors remain half-t(3, 0, 2.5).

Variance-component priors now half-t(3, 0, 2.5) specified article. prior-sensitivity selector available. intercept prior mean SD supplied data, defaulting design-weighted logit prevalence SD 0.5. title: bhfvar 0.5.0

Estimand B now averages individual probabilities include realized stratum PSU effects, adds within-domain mixture variance term. previous marginal approximation removed. * subtracts population-weighted mean sampling variance ’s -domain variance floored zero. Added signed diagnostic gaps , *, B. Latent-scale SDs ICCs reported separately probability-scale estimands.
